A TCP SYN Flood attack works by exploiting the TCP handshake process. In this type of attack, an adversary sends a large number of SYN (synchronize) requests to a target server, but does not complete the handshake by sending the final ACK (acknowledgment) packet. This results in the server allocating resources for each half-open connection, which can lead to resource exhaustion and denial of service (DoS) for legitimate users. The attack effectively overwhelms the server, reducing its availability and functionality [Source 1].
